title: AWS managed policy update
description: Lambda added a new AWS managed policy (AWSLambdaNetworkConnectorOperatorPolicy) to grant permissions to create and administer elastic network interface (ENI) resources managed by the Lambda Network Connector. For more information, see Lambda updates to AWS managed policies.

title: AWS managed policy update
description: Lambda updated the AWSLambdaManagedEC2ResourceOperator managed policy to add Amazon CloudWatch permissions (logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents). For details, see Lambda updates to AWS managed policies.

title: Permissions checks for EC2 Fast Launch
description: Added guidance on how Amazon EC2 validates your permissions when you enable EC2 Fast Launch with a launch template, including a security consideration for using the $Latest or $Default launch template version.

title: EFA support for static capacity in EKS Auto Mode
description: Added support for configuring EFA network interfaces on EKS Auto Mode NodeClass resources. You can now statically define network interfaces at instance launch for high-performance distributed training and inference workloads.

title: AWS managed policy updates
description: Added new API action ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes to AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy to enable the EBS CSI Driver to dynamically retrieve volume limit/card information at runtime.

title: Internet Monitor publishes local health events to Amazon EventBridge
description: Internet Monitor now publishes local health events to Amazon EventBridge, in addition to overall (global) health events. Local health events have an impact type of LOCAL_AVAILABILITY or LOCAL_PERFORMANCE.

title: 8 new AWS SDK service integrations
description: Added AWS DevOps Agent Service, AWS Interconnect, AWS Marketplace Discovery, AWS Security Agent, AWS Sustainability, AWS User Experience Customization, Amazon S3 Files, Amazon SimpleDB v2.

title: Update to AWS managed policy
description: The AWSSecretsManagerClientReadOnlyAccess managed policy now includes BatchGetSecretValue and ListSecrets permissions. For information, see Secrets Manager updates to AWS managed policies.

title: Amazon CloudFront announces API support for flat-rate pricing plans
description:
Starting today, customers can subscribe and manage flat-rate pricing plans programmatically using the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, CloudFormation, CDK, or the PricingPlanManager API.

CloudFront flat-rate plans give you one monthly price covering global content delivery, WAF, DDoS, DNS, logging, and edge compute, with no usage-based overage charges regardless of traffic spikes or attacks. title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-West)
description: The Web Search built-in server-side tool on Amazon Bedrock is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-West), helping bring grounded web results to compliance-sensitive government and public-sector workloads. Web Search helps supported OpenAI GPT models ground responses with information from the web. Responses include citations to the sources the model used so users can trace each claim back to its web origin. title: AWS Config now supports 60 new resource types
description:
AWS Config now supports 60 additional AWS resource types across key services including Amazon Bedrock,  Amazon EC2, Amazon SageMaker, and AWS Organizations. This expansion provides greater coverage over your AWS environment, enabling you to more effectively discover, assess, audit, and remediate an even broader range of resources.

title: AWS Lambda now supports SnapStart for container image functions
description:
Starting today, AWS Lambda supports SnapStart for functions packaged as container images, reducing startup times from several seconds to as low as sub-second. Lambda SnapStart is an opt-in capability that makes it easier for you to build highly responsive and scalable applications without provisioning resources or implementing complex performance optimizations.

title: Amazon Cognito now supports machine-to-machine authorization without a user pool domain
description:
Amazon Cognito now supports the GetClientToken API operation, enabling app clients to obtain access tokens for machine-to-machine (M2M) authorization directly through the AWS SDK, CLI, or API — without configuring a user pool domain. This gives you an additional path to authorize service-to-service communication for applications, microservices, and automated workloads.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore expands to two new regions
description:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available in two additional AWS Regions: US West (N. California) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the platform to build, connect, and optimize agents. It helps engineers ship agents fast with any framework and any model, connect them to enterprise systems and tools, and optimize them continuously, with security enforced at the infrastructure layer that agents can't bypass.
